svg.title: Most of the 93 dB gap at the NASA station is one step: from a drone placed perfectly in the beam to real traffic (55 dB)

cc:Work.dc:title: Most of the 93 dB gap at the NASA station is one step: from a drone placed perfectly in the beam to real traffic (55 dB)
cc:Work.dc:description: Waterfall chart from +43 dB for one drone following the beam to -50 dB under normal conditions at the Wallops NEN station. The largest step, 55 dB, is going from a perfectly placed drone to random traffic. Counting over all time gives -60 dB; a 20 dB apportionment gives -34 dB. Both stay below the allowance at 0 dB.
